review_basis: registered MEXT Physics Basics/Chemistry Basics source version and printed-page locators
semantic distinctness, direct source support and educational value

decisions.rationale: Temperature increase and stronger thermal motion is a direct foundational proposition.
This is the exact inverse of C001 and tests the same answer-defining temperature/thermal-motion relationship without adding a distinct misconception or decision boundary.
The cited three-state subsection supports state changes, but the locator as persisted does not independently establish the closed-system mass-conservation proposition used to define the answer.
decisions.resume_condition: Bind the mass-conservation claim to an explicit registered source/locator, or rewrite to a state-change proposition directly stated by the cited subsection.

decisions.rationale: Melting point as the solid/liquid boundary is direct and independently testable.
Boiling point as the liquid/gas boundary is distinct from melting point and source-explicit.
The particle-model relationship between thermal motion and interparticle forces is a useful synthesis proposition.
Melting as physical change directly tests substance identity versus state.
Decomposition is a separate chemical-change definition, not a wording variant of C007.
Internal energy is a direct foundational term relevant to heat and work.
Kelvin as the SI unit of absolute temperature is precise and distinct.
Natural heat transfer from higher to lower temperature is a core directional boundary.
Equality of heat lost and gained in an isolated pair is a distinct conservation relationship.
Heat capacity and temperature-change comparison is a high-value quantitative decision.
Specific heat under fixed mass and heat is distinct from total heat capacity and uses an explicit relationship.
Latent heat is a direct state-change term and does not collide with C004/C005.
Thermal expansion tests dimension/volume change rather than mass change.
Rapid gas compression converting work into internal-energy/temperature rise is a distinct application.
Mechanical work dissipating into heat is related but materially distinct from gas compression.
Density as a characteristic property is source-explicit and relevant to material identification.
Atomic structure is a direct matter-foundation proposition and absent from canonical 51.

collision_review.note: C002 is rejected as an inverse duplicate of C001. C003 requires a direct mass-conservation source binding. No accepted B5 candidate materially collides with canonical 51 or accepted B4/B6 propositions.

source_review_scope: This gate checks source registration, locator reproducibility and answer-binding completeness. Final canonical source verification remains separate.
